hook: Marc Raibert is a roboticist known as the founder of Boston Dynamics. He held research and faculty positions at Carnegie Mellon University and MIT, where he ran the MIT Leg Lab studying dynamic, legged locomotion in robots. In 1992 he spun the lab's work out of MIT to found Boston Dynamics, joined soon after by Robert Playter. Under his leadership the company built a series of dynamically balancing robots, including BigDog, Cheetah, Atlas, and Spot, that became widely recognized demonstrations of legged robotics. Boston Dynamics passed through ownership by Google's X division, SoftBank Group, and Hyundai Motor Company over the following decades, and Raibert stepped back from the CEO role while remaining involved with the company. He now serves as Executive Director of the Robotics and AI Institute, which he leads from offices in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Zurich, Switzerland.
